sent_to_model:
so my blog needs a post and it's not a fun one. Basically my van almost caught fire last week, the inverter cable melted while I was drying a dog. Everyone's fine but I'm off the road for weeks and kind of losing my mind. Tasha is literally about to pay a deposit with the same guy who built mine, so I want to write it up properly for her and the other groomer girls who read my blog. Like the actual electrical stuff, what went wrong, what the electrician showed me, what to check on your own van. I'm not an electrician so don't make me sound like one, but I want the numbers right. here's everything I wrote down after she left

- Wed Oct 28, around 2:15pm, in a client's driveway in Bedford, drying Moose (Bernese) on high
- setup - 3000W inverter, two 200Ah lithium batteries, 12V, built by Coastline Van Fitouts (Darren) spring 2025
- the cable from battery to inverter was 4 AWG. electrician (Priya, Sackville Marine Electric) says should've been 2/0 for 3000W at 12V
- dryer pulls like 1800-2000W, plus the water heater sometimes. at 12V thats 150-250 amps through that cable
- the lug on the positive end was crimped with like pliers or a hammer, not a proper crimper. heat-shrink was hiding it
- fuse was a 300A ANL but it was mounted like 90cm from the battery, Priya said should be within 18cm-ish
- no smoke detector in the back, just the one in the cab that came with the van
- repair quote 4,200 dollars, rewire main runs + new fuse block + class T fuse. 3 weeks min, parts on order
- cancelled 31 appointments so far. insurance says maybe, adjuster coming Thursday
- Darren hasn't answered 3 texts and an email
- smelled hot plastic first, thought it was the dryer motor. then saw smoke coming out of the bench seat where the batteries are
- killed the battery switch, got Moose out the side door still damp, he was thrilled honestly
- used the extinguisher a bit, not even sure I needed to. lug was black and the jacket had melted back like 3cm
- Priya pulled up my damage photos next to thermal camera shots of her own van running the same kind of load, hers barely gets warm. the difference is wild
- Moose's mom brought me a coffee and sat with me on her steps while I shook
- I trusted the build cause it looked tidy. tidy is not the same as right
- I'm not trying to trash Darren publicly, just say the facts, people can decide
- honestly scared, my whole income is that van, rent is due the 1st
- everyone should own a cheap infrared thermometer, I got one for 40 bucks at Canadian Tire
- Tasha especially - get her to ask any builder for cable sizes and fuse specs in writing before deposit
- a checklist people can actually do on their own van with the power off
- say clearly I'm not an electrician, get a pro to look
- end with an update on where I'm at and that I'll post again when van's back

(About me: mobile dog groomer, 28, Halifax, Canada. Length: it should come to roughly 2,000-4,000 words.)

must_cover: Recounts the incident and electrical faults, including Priya comparing damage photos with thermal images of her own van under similar load.
Explicitly states the narrator is not an electrician and explains the electrical numbers without claiming professional expertise.
Urges Tasha to obtain cable sizes and fuse specifications in writing before paying a deposit.
Gives a power-off checklist and advises getting a qualified electrician.
Updates readers on repairs and promises a further post when the van returns.
